title: A boolean filter argument may reference two columns of the same table

source.quote: DAX now supports expressions where multiple columns belonging to the same table are part of the predicate expression in a CALCULATE filter argument.
source.supports: since March 2021 a predicate may use several columns of one table; it is run as FILTER over ALL of those columns

source.quote: It can reference only columns of one table, but it can use more than one column of that table.
source.supports: DAX Guide: one table, more than one column allowed

source.quote: They can reference only a single column.
source.supports: the CALCULATETABLE reference page still states the older single-column rule

source.quote: However, you cannot write a single filter argument referencing two different columns
source.supports: this older SQLBI article says such a predicate cannot be written

derivation: Blue or Vehicles: Lock (Blue), Bike and Scooter (Vehicles). 80 + 400 + BLANK = 480.
alternative: Under the older rule (a boolean filter argument can reference only a single column) the query is an error: the expression contains columns from multiple columns of a table filter expression, which is not allowed.
notes: SUM of a fixed decimal (currency) column is taken to be a fixed decimal, as in the seed cases.
